parsed.title: Router's `rows:` line lists every open row, not the selected ones
parsed.detail: `main()` computes `selected` per route but `print()` is called with `rows: rowIds` where `const rowIds = rows.map((row) => row.id)` — every open row, including fold/decision rows. The replan contract (`skills/replan-findings/SKILL.md` Bounded intake step 2) says "The `rows:` line names the findings … Read exactly those rows", and `PHASE_APPEND.md` says "For every finding the router's `rows:` line selected". On the unit-37 fixture the router prints `rows: F83 F85 F88 F90 F92` (test AC5) while F90 is a `fold` row and F88/F92 are replan — the test itself asserts the union, so the contract's "selected rows only" is violated by the code and pinned by the test.

parsed.title: `readSetFor` base for `plan-from-issue` is wrong directory
parsed.detail: `print({... readSet: readSetFor("docs/fix", [], ["README.md"]) })` — `readSetFor(unitDir, rows, base)` builds `${unitDir}/${name}`, so this yields `docs/fix/README.md`, which is fine, but the `unit` field is the bare issue number and `status: "pending"` is hardcoded rather than read from the fix index row (the fixture row is `pending`, but a real `in-progress` issue would still print `pending`). The status is a claimed fact not derived from the index.

parsed.title: `fixIndexIssues` regex matches any `#N` in the first cell, including PR links
parsed.detail: `/issues\/(\d+)|#(\d+)/` over `line.split("|")[1]` — the fix index's first cell is the issue link, but the same regex also matches a `#N` in a topic cell if the first cell is empty, and more importantly `fixIndexStatus` uses `new RegExp(\`issues/${number}\\b|#${number}\\b\`)` which will match `#224` inside `#2240`? No — `\b` after digits is fine. The real issue: `fixIndexIssues` adds the number from `#(\d+)` even when the cell is a PR link `[#225](.../pull/225)`, so a fix index row whose first cell is a PR (not an issue) would be treated as a tracked issue. Low confidence; noting as low.

parsed.title: `roadmapStatus`/`fixIndexStatus` split on `·` but the roadmap status cell is `done · [#225](...)`
parsed.detail: `cells[3].split("·")[0].trim()` — for the roadmap the status is column 3 (index 3 after the leading empty cell), which is correct for `| NN | Slug | Status | Depends on | Summary |`. But `fixIndexStatus` uses `cells[3]` for `| Issue | Topic | Status | Notes |` — that is the **Notes** column, not Status. The fix index status is `cells[2]`. So `node scripts/unit-route.mjs 224` would print `status: <notes text>` instead of `done`.

parsed.title: `openRows` requires `cells.length < 7` but `cellsOf(...).slice(1,-1)` drops the trailing empty cell
parsed.detail: A well-formed row `| F1 | ... | no |` splits to `['', 'F1', ..., 'no', '']`; `.slice(1,-1)` gives 7 cells — OK. But a row with a trailing `|` and no space still works. The `VF-` skip is correct. However `isOpen` treats `''` as closed, so a row with a missing `folded` cell is silently dropped rather than reported — a ledger row with a malformed folded cell is invisible to the router, contradicting the sensor's "named, never silent" discipline.

parsed.title: `readSuggestions` uses `unit.issue` for fix units but `unit.id` for features
parsed.detail: `const command = unit.kind === "fix" ? \`/plan-fix ${unit.issue}\` : \`/plan-feature ${unit.id}\`;` — the test asserts `/plan-fix 91` for a fix unit whose folder is `91-alpha`, so `unit.issue` must be `91`. But the router's own `command` for a fix unit is `/plan-fix ${unit.number}` (the folder prefix). If `unit.issue` and `unit.number` diverge (e.g. a multi-issue fix unit whose primary is the lowest number but the folder is named after it), the sensor and router name different commands for the same unit — the exact "two destinations" defect the unit exists to remove.

parsed.title: `readSuggestions` duplicates the router's `PLAN_ROUTE` regex instead of importing it
parsed.detail: `const PLAN_ROUTE = /replan[- ]in[- ]unit|owned by plan|plan owner|plan-owner/i;` is declared in both `scripts/unit-route.mjs` and `scripts/workflow-status.mjs`. The SPEC's own root cause #4 and the `normative-drift` test claim "the class→destination decision is the router's" and "neither may invent a fourth destination" — but the sensor re-implements the classifier, so a future edit to one regex silently diverges. The drift test only checks token presence, not that the sensor delegates.

parsed.title: `next.suggested` is attached after `resolveNext` but the schema field may be required/typed
parsed.detail: `next.suggested = nextSuggested;` mutates the object returned by `resolveNext`. The test `validateEnvelope(...).ok === true` passes, so the schema accepts it. But `SENSOR_SIGNALS.md` step 13 says `next.suggested[]` is "One entry per fired trigger" and lists five trigger kinds (review checkpoint, adversarial, closure, replan, fold) — the implementation only ever emits replan or fold, never the other three. The doc claims a broader surface than the code emits.

parsed.title: Replan contract says "read only the read-set paths" but the router's read-set omits the ledger itself for replan
parsed.detail: `readSetFor` base for replan is `["review-findings.md", "SPEC.md", "ACCEPTANCE.md"]` — good. But `citedPaths` only keeps paths that `exists()` under the project root; the unit-37 fixture's `docs/LOGS.md` is excluded because it is cited only by a folded row (test asserts this). However the replan contract's step 2 says "The `rows:` line names the findings … Read exactly those rows" — and the router's `rows:` line includes F90 (a fold row) whose cited path is `docs/LOGS.md`, which is *not* in the read set. So the contract instructs reading a row whose cited path the router deliberately excluded.

parsed.title: Replan exemption runs before the status gate but the Product-review gate still runs
parsed.detail: The exemption says "skip the STOP and load the replan contract". But `plan-feature/SKILL.md` turn contract box 2 says "Then the Product-review gate ran: no current `spec-review-pass` receipt … → STOP". A replan on an in-flight unit has no fresh `spec-review-pass` (the SPEC was already reviewed at design time, but the replan appends phases to the *plan*, not the product half). The exemption only skips the *status* STOP, not the Product-review gate — so a replan route would still be blocked by the Product gate, which the replan contract never mentions. The two documents disagree on whether the replan route is reachable.

parsed.title: `plan-fix` replan entry runs the router "for the target unit" but `plan-fix` takes issue numbers, not unit slugs
parsed.detail: `argument-hint: <issue-number> [<issue-number> …]` and the input section says "One or more GitHub issue numbers". The new step 7 says "Only when `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <N>` prints `route: replan` for the target unit" — but `<N>` is an issue number, and the router's `resolveUnit` matches on folder prefix/slug, not issue number. `node scripts/unit-route.mjs 224` would match the folder `224-deterministic-replan-routing` only if the folder prefix equals the issue number, which it does here, but for a multi-issue fix unit the folder is named after the primary and the other issue numbers would not resolve. The invocation as documented fails for the multi-issue case the skill explicitly supports.

parsed.title: Replan detection says "when the target resolves to an existing unit folder" but ingest happens first
parsed.detail: The new paragraph is placed *before* step 1 ("Ingest all inputs"), and says "When the target resolves to an existing unit folder, run the router first". But resolving the target to a unit folder requires reading the fix index / roadmap, which is part of ingest. The ordering is circular: you cannot know the unit folder before ingesting the issue. The router itself resolves by folder prefix, so `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <issue-number>` works only when the folder prefix equals the issue number.

parsed.title: AC7 validator greps 14 files but the census claims 8 skill + 6 tutorial = 14; the SPEC Scope lists 8 skill + 3 tutorial pairs = 14 files, consistent — but AC7's grep list omits `skills/review-change/SKILL.md`
parsed.detail: AC7's grep list: `PERSIST_AND_DECIDE.md`, `OUTPUT_AND_GUARDRAILS.md`, `CLASSIFY.md`, `review-implementation/SKILL.md`, `triage-issue/SKILL.md`, `REVIEW_FINDING_PROCESS.md`, `FOLD_PROCESS.md`, `fold-findings/SKILL.md` (8 skill files) + 6 tutorial files. But `skills/review-change/SKILL.md`'s Relationship section still says "`replan-in-unit` adds user-confirmed phases" with no router mention (visible in the current content at tip). The SPEC's own Decision 8 says `review-change/SKILL.md:157` is a "class definition or summary that names no destination" and stays untouched — but the current text *does* name a destination ("adds user-confirmed phases") without the router, contradicting AC7's "no converged surface sends a replan row to the executor or the fold" only if that surface is counted. It is not counted, so AC7 passes by exclusion while the surface still carries the old phrasing.

parsed.title: SPEC Status says `pending` but progress.md and fix index say `done`
parsed.detail: SPEC `## Status` section: "`pending` · `in-progress` · `done` (built, PR open …)" — this is the legend, not the value. The actual status is not stated in the SPEC; the fix index row says `done · [#225]` and progress.md P8 says "Unit status: **done**". The SPEC's Status section is a legend with no recorded value, so a reader cannot tell the unit's state from the SPEC. Minor but the SPEC is the source of truth.

parsed.title: SPEC `## Status` records ACCEPTANCE blob `0dd2747…` but progress.md cycle-2 receipt records `b6dc545…`
parsed.detail: SPEC Status: "`git hash-object docs/fix/224-deterministic-replan-routing/ACCEPTANCE.md` → `0dd2747222ce25617ffcf6eae851035a215d6504`". progress.md cycle-2 receipt: "Acceptance manifest blob re-computed: … → `b6dc545edf96e99a6d0081eadac298124c7ac592` — matches the value recorded in the SPEC `## Status` after the re-freeze ✓". The cycle-2 receipt claims `b6dc545` matches the SPEC, but the SPEC at tip records `0dd2747`. The cycle-3 receipt records `0dd2747` and says it matches. So the cycle-2 receipt's claim is false against the tip bytes — either the SPEC was re-frozen between cycle 2 and 3 (artrev-0003) and the cycle-2 receipt is stale-but-honest, or the cycle-2 receipt is wrong. The cycle-2 receipt says "matches the value recorded in the SPEC `## Status` after the re-freeze" — at cycle 2 the SPEC recorded `b6dc545`; artrev-0003 re-froze to `0dd2747`. The receipts are internally consistent across cycles, but the SPEC's Status section only records the latest blob, so a reader cannot verify the cycle-2 claim. Not a defect per se.

parsed.title: P8 claims `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → 282 tests but the unit adds 14+53+17 tests to a suite that was previously smaller
parsed.detail: P8: "`NODE_PATH=… node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → exit 0 · 282 tests, 282 pass, 0 fail." The unit adds `scripts/unit-route.test.mjs` (14 cases), 3 new sensor tests, 1 new drift test. If the pre-unit suite was ~264, 282 is plausible. Not a defect.

parsed.title: P8 says a version pin was "maintained" by advancing `fold-findings` pin from 1.4.0 to 1.5.0
parsed.detail: `scripts/review-loop-discipline.test.mjs:10j` pinned `fold-findings`'s exact version to 1.4.0. P8 advanced it to 1.5.0 "with the assertion unchanged in strength — a version fact, not a weakened check". But the test's own comment says "The exact pin is maintained on every later bump" — this converts a one-time contract pin into a moving target, so the pin no longer detects an *unintended* bump. The original pin's purpose (feature 30's one-time contract) is defeated. The SPEC's quality floor says "Do not remove, skip, loosen, or rewrite a validator to manufacture PASS" — advancing a version pin to match the new version is exactly rewriting a validator to pass.

parsed.title: `replan-findings` budget entry has no `mainEstimateMax`/`mainLinesMax` override but the skill's main file is 92 lines
parsed.detail: The entry only sets `referenceSources`. The defaults are `mainEstimateMax: 2800`, `mainLinesMax: 240`. The skill's `SKILL.md` is 92 lines / ~3.5KB → ~875 est, under budget. Fine. But the entry's `referenceSources` note says "measured within the default reference budget" — the reference `PHASE_APPEND.md` is 89 lines / ~3.5KB → ~875 est, under 2200. Fine. No defect.

parsed.title: Route ceilings re-based to `ceil(measured × 1.10)` but the SPEC's Rules say "Skills stay within their context budgets"
parsed.detail: P8 raised four route ceilings (plan-feature:issue/scoped, plan-fix:issue, review-change:adversarial/default-backend/default-web/synthesize) to `ceil(measured × 1.10)`. The SPEC's Rules section says "Skills stay within their context budgets. The new main file must satisfy the manifest's defaults (`mainEstimateMax: 2800`, `mainLinesMax: 240`)." The route ceilings are a different budget, and the repo's declared rule (visible in the JSON's own `sources` notes from prior units) is that ceilings are re-based at the declared headroom with a named growth source — which P8 did. Not a defect.

parsed.title: Internal-step count bumped 18 → 19 but the prose enumerates only 18 named steps

parsed.title: Portable prompt says "16 user-facing skills + 13 internal steps" but SKILLS.md says 19 + 19

parsed.title: Doc says `replan-in-unit` runs the router and the planner appends phases, but the router's `next:` for a replan is `/plan-feature <slug>` or `/plan-fix <n>` — not a phase-append command
parsed.detail: The doc: "run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`; its `route: replan` line names the planner (`/plan-feature` for a feature, `/plan-fix` for a fix), which appends user-confirmed phase(s) to the unit's SPEC `## Phases` ledger". But `plan-feature`'s own redirect gate STOPS on a `planned`/`in-progress` roadmap row — the replan exemption in `ROUTING.md` is supposed to skip that STOP, but the exemption is only in `ROUTING.md`, and `plan-feature/SKILL.md`'s turn contract still requires the Product-review gate. The doc presents the path as working end-to-end; the code path has an unresolved gate.

parsed.title: Spanish doc has the same end-to-end claim

parsed.detail: "`replan-in-unit` runs `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`, whose `route: replan` line names the planner that appends new user-confirmed phases to the unit's SPEC (fresh `/review-plan` first)". Same as REVIEW_AND_CLASSIFY: the Product-review gate in `plan-feature` is not addressed.

parsed.title: `→ Next:` block says the router "prints `route: replan`" but the router prints `route: replan` only when a plan-owned row exists; a `replan-in-unit` finding that is *not* plan-owned (e.g. a source-owned replan) would route to `fold` or `decision`
parsed.detail: The block: "any finding routed replan-in-unit or owned by plan? → `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` prints `route: replan` and names the planner". But `replan-in-unit` is a *class* (size too large to fold), not necessarily plan-owned. `CLASSIFY.md` says a `replan-in-unit` finding keeps its fix-now class and its owning stage can be `source` or `plan`. A source-owned `replan-in-unit` finding would be routed by the router to `fold` (since its route cell says `replan-in-unit` — wait, `PLAN_ROUTE` regex matches `replan-in-unit`, so it *would* route to replan). Actually the regex matches the route cell text, so any `replan-in-unit` row routes to replan regardless of owning stage. So the block is correct. But `CLASSIFY.md`'s owning-stage table says a `source`-owned finding folds locally — a `replan-in-unit` source-owned finding would be routed to replan by the router, contradicting the owning-stage table. The two documents disagree on whether a source-owned replan-in-unit finding folds or replans.

parsed.title: Owning-stage table says `source` folds locally, but a `replan-in-unit` source-owned finding is routed to replan by the router
parsed.detail: The table: "| `source` | fold locally: `/fold-findings`, then re-run `/review-change` on the changed HEAD | — |". But the router's `PLAN_ROUTE` regex matches the route cell `replan-in-unit` regardless of owning stage, so a source-owned `replan-in-unit` finding routes to `replan`, not `fold`. The owning-stage table and the router disagree.

parsed.title: Freeze-batch routes to the router but the router's `route: replan` line names the planner — the fold's `→ Next:` block says "the planner it names re-cuts the plan, then `/review-plan` before `/execute-phase`"
parsed.detail: The freeze-batch branch: "`node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` → the planner it names re-cuts the plan, then `/review-plan` before `/execute-phase` on this unit". But the router's `next:` line for a replan is `/plan-feature <slug>` or `/plan-fix <n>` — it does not name `/review-plan` or `/execute-phase`. The fold's block adds steps the router does not print. Minor, but the block claims the router names the full sequence.

parsed.title: `→ Next:` block still has a `REPLAN` branch that says "confirm all proposed SPEC phases, then /execute-phase on this same branch" — contradicting the new freeze-batch branch
parsed.detail: The Done-when block: "· any REPLAN (<F1> + <F2> + …) → confirm all proposed SPEC phases, then /execute-phase on this same branch". The new freeze-batch branch says route through the router and `/review-plan` first. The two branches in the same file disagree: one says confirm-then-execute, the other says router-then-review-plan-then-execute. The `REPLAN` branch was not updated.

parsed.title: Step 9 says "run the router" but step 1 says `replan-in-unit` rows emit `REPLAN` and stay on the same branch
parsed.detail: Step 1: "`replan-in-unit` rows emit `REPLAN`; they stay on the same SPEC/branch/PR and never become issues." Step 9: "run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` — its `route: replan` line names the planner … that appends the proposed phases". Step 1 says the row emits REPLAN and stays; step 9 says run the router. The two steps describe different flows for the same row.

parsed.title: Step 4 says "ask the user to continue manually with `/execute-phase <unit> P<n>`" but step 3 says a fresh `/review-plan` must pass first
parsed.detail: Step 3: "the fresh `/review-plan <unit>` that must pass before execution". Step 4: "After a replan, ask the user to continue manually with `/execute-phase <unit> P<n>`". Step 4 omits the `/review-plan` step, so a user following step 4 would execute without the fresh review.

parsed.title: Relationship diagram says `unit-route → plan-feature / plan-fix (replan)` but the prose says the router names the planner and a fresh `/review-plan` before execution
parsed.detail: The diagram: "or unit-route → plan-feature / plan-fix (replan)". The prose: "runs `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`: its `route: replan` line names the planner …, with new `P<n>` phases appended to the same unit and a fresh `/review-plan` before execution." The diagram omits the `/review-plan` step. Minor.

parsed.title: Relationship section still says "`replan-in-unit` adds user-confirmed phases" with no router mention
parsed.detail: The Relationship section: "`fix-now` is routed to the unit's fold cycle — a separate `/fold-findings` invocation, never run by this review; `replan-in-unit` adds user-confirmed phases, and independent work becomes proposals." The SPEC's Decision 8 says `review-change/SKILL.md:157` is a "class definition or summary that names no destination" and stays untouched — but the text *does* name a destination ("adds user-confirmed phases") without the router. The unit's own AC7 says "no converged surface sends a replan row to the executor or the fold" — this surface sends it to neither, but it also does not name the router, so a reader following it would not know to run the router. The SPEC's exclusion is defensible but the surface is not fully converged.

parsed.title: New drift test asserts the sensor names `/plan-feature`, `/plan-fix`, `/fold-findings` but does not assert the sensor delegates to the router
parsed.detail: The test: "for (const token of ["replan-in-unit", "/plan-feature", "/plan-fix", "/fold-findings"]) { assert.ok(sensor.includes(token), …) }" and "for (const token of ["/plan-feature", "/plan-fix", "/fold-findings"]) { assert.ok(router.includes(token), …) }". This only checks token presence, not that the sensor's class→destination mapping matches the router's. A sensor that hardcodes a different mapping (e.g. sends a plan-owned row to `/fold-findings`) would still pass. The test's own comment says "neither may invent a fourth destination for the same class" — but the test does not verify the mapping, only the token set.

parsed.title: AC5 test asserts `rows: F83 F85 F88 F90 F92` — includes F90, a fold row
parsed.detail: The test: `assert.equal(rowLine(result.stdout), "F83 F85 F88 F90 F92", "the plan-routed open rows, no id passed in")`. F90's route cell is `fold: relocate …` (a fold row), not a replan row. The test's own description says "the plan-routed open rows" but the assertion includes a fold row. The router's `rows:` line lists all open rows, not the selected ones — the test pins the bug.

parsed.title: AC2 test asserts read-set count 23 for `40-cited-paths` but the fixture has 20 cited files + 3 unit surfaces = 23
parsed.detail: The test: `assert.equal(set.count, 23, "3 unit surfaces + 20 distinct cited files")`. The fixture `40-cited-paths/review-findings.md` cites `src/file-1.txt` through `src/file-20.txt` (20 files) plus the unit's `review-findings.md`, `SPEC.md`, `ACCEPTANCE.md` (3) = 23. Correct. But the read-set cap is 12, and the test asserts `set.entries.length === 12` and `set.remainder === 11`. 12 + 11 = 23. Correct.

parsed.title: AC12 test asserts `!result.stdout.includes(longId)` but the router's `rows:` line includes the truncated id `F9-AAAA…`
parsed.detail: The test: `assert.ok(!result.stdout.includes(longId), "the long id is truncated by the sanitizer")` and `assert.match(result.stdout, /F9-AAAA/, "the id keeps its truncated prefix")`. The long id is `F9-${'A'.repeat(400)}`; the sanitizer truncates to 160 chars, so the output contains `F9-AAAA…` (159 A's + ellipsis). The test's first assertion `!includes(longId)` passes because the full 400-A string is not present. Correct.

parsed.title: `sanitize` truncates to `CELL_MAX - 1` chars + ellipsis = 160 chars total, but the test asserts `F9-AAAA` prefix — fine
parsed.detail: No defect.

parsed.title: `fingerprint` hashes `{unit, status, route, rows, readSet}` but not `openCount` or `command`
parsed.detail: `const record = { unit, status, route, rows, readSet };` — `openCount` and `command` are printed but not fingerprinted. Two runs with the same unit/status/route/rows/readSet but different `command` (e.g. a fix unit whose `unit.kind` changed) would have the same fingerprint. Minor.

parsed.title: `main` calls `print` with `rows: rowIds` but `print` destructures `rows` and uses `rows.length` for the `rows:` line — the `openCount` is `rows.length` (all open rows), not the selected count
parsed.detail: `print({ ..., openCount: rows.length, rows: rowIds, ... })` — `openCount` is the total open rows, `rows` is the total open row ids. The `rows:` line prints all open ids. The `open-rows:` line prints the total. Neither reflects the selected rows. The replan contract's "Read exactly those rows" is unfulfillable from the output.

parsed.title: `readSuggestions` is called for every unit but `unit.issue` may be undefined for feature units
parsed.detail: `const command = unit.kind === "fix" ? \`/plan-fix ${unit.issue}\` : \`/plan-feature ${unit.id}\`;` — for a feature unit, `unit.issue` is not used. For a fix unit, `unit.issue` must be defined. The test passes for a fix unit with `unit.issue = 91`. But if a fix unit's `unit.issue` is undefined (e.g. a fix folder without a matching fix-index row), the command becomes `/plan-fix undefined`. The router's `fixIndexStatus` returns `null` for an unmatched fix, and the router's `command` uses `unit.number` (the folder prefix), not `unit.issue`. The sensor and router disagree on the fix command's argument.

parsed.title: `readOpenRows` skips `VF-` rows but the sensor's `readFixNow` previously did not — a behavior change not mentioned in the changelog
